findings.reason: without a named caller or a named owning plan the node must either edit a file it was not granted or record a false ownership claim, and a false allowlist entry hides the very unreached module the invariant exists to catch.
findings.text: §51's only route to green on `test_every_module_is_reached` is a production caller for `reckon.crew.plan_coordinator` and `reckon.crew.station_store` (grep shows no module imports either), but its write paths grant only those two modules and the test files, and the alternative — adding both to the test's `ALLOWLIST` — requires naming the plan that owns wiring them, which the section never settles

findings.reason: the section's first step re-confirms the id at its own base and the Done-when adds "passes in a worktree whose path differs from the main checkout's", so the node measures the property directly and the log's header only governs how the citation reads.
findings.text: the §52 Why rests the "passes in the main checkout" half of its evidence on `pathcheck-main.log`, a log that names neither its revision, tree nor command, has no `EXIT=` line, and lists only the two ids that failed, so the id it is cited for cannot be confirmed from it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the §52 Why's claim that the id "passes in the main checkout" cites `~/.cache/reckon-suite-census/pathcheck-main.log`, which carries no `# rev=`/tree/command header, no `EXIT=` line, and names only its two failures ("2 failed, 4 passed"), so the four passing ids — the §52 id among them — are not named anywhere in the file it cites.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — every section names a base arm, per-id negative controls that mutate the production code the test pins (explicitly refusing "restore the old expectation" as a control), logs naming revision/tree/literal command and ending in `EXIT=`, and ruff on the staged paths; the id counts and id sets match the cited census failures exactly (§41 14, §42 8, §43 6, §44 6, §45 10, §46 12, §47 11, §48 9, §49 11, §50 6, §51 9, §52 1).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs are required under the run directory (a durable path under the run's own `logs/`), and the census evidence the Whys cite resolves: `~/.cache/reckon-suite-census/c8a082c99e3023b61c438143e898bd0039315149-rerun/rerun.log` and `~/.cache/reckon-suite-census/verify-684c1caa61836074490c2589abacf828be76a00a/verify.log` both exist, and the verify log ends `120 failed, 10 passed ... EXIT=1`, matching the "120 still fail" claim.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the sections introduce no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags into symbols or files; the Why prose cites commit subjects and slugs as provenance, which is the plan's own record rather than a name carried into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §51's mechanism cannot produce its done-when inside its declared write paths (`tests/test_every_module_is_reached.py` fails on `reckon.crew.plan_coordinator` and `reckon.crew.station_store` being "unreached and not in the allowlist", and neither a production caller nor the owning plan is granted by the write paths); the root-cause check passes for the other eleven sections, whose stated causes match the recorded tracebacks: §41's `crew redispatch` exits 10 with the `crew resume --backend` tombstone; §42's row lacks `manifest_status`; §43's rendered node gains `lift_preference`; §46's discard leaves no record and the picker-hold call count is 3 where 2 are expected; §47's raising sweep emits 0 where 1 is expected; §48's sweep dry run resumes `[]`; §50's placement field loads without `FlightConfigError`; §49's refusal carries no `refused_ops`; §51's prefix literal is indeed spelled in `reckon/crew/plan_coordinator.py` (line 14) against the single owner in `reckon/crew/recovery_vocabulary.py:147`, and `reckon/crew/station_store.py:200` calls `date.fromisoformat` directly.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of the twelve sections carries one deliverable shape and one verdict: re-freeze the listed ids to the intended contract, or return an id as blocked with the commit and the unintended change. §46 and §47 keep the id bundles the earlier review flagged, but their Why now names the single mechanism each bundle shares (one admission vocabulary; follower/sweep/producer progress), so one verdict covers the section rather than two independent deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s41–s52 declare no depends-on, informs or gates and none is claimed for them; the plan's only section edge is `plan-section-depends-on` carrying s32, and the §50 ordering constraint is declared on the consumer's side (`a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline`), as the earlier review's declined wiring finding records.
